questions.q: A distribution has a long tail toward high values, like order amounts where a few customers spend enormously. What is it called?
questions.explain: The direction of skew is the direction of the long tail, so a long tail toward high values is right-skewed.

questions.q: In right-skewed data the mean is typically:
questions.explain: The long right tail pulls the mean above the median; in the lesson, 30.3 versus 21.3.

questions.q: A mixed dataset of two groups (centers near 20 and 60) had a mean of 40.0 and a median of 40.1, yet almost no values near 40. What does this illustrate?
options: Summary numbers can hide a bimodal shape, so plot the data
The mean is always the best summary
questions.explain: The center fell in a gap between two peaks; only a chart or a subgroup question reveals that.

questions.q: In pandas, what does Series.kurt() return?
options: Excess kurtosis, where about 0 corresponds to a normal distribution
questions.explain: pandas reports excess kurtosis (Fisher definition), so a normal distribution is near 0 and heavier tails give larger values.

questions.q: Why might you apply np.log1p to a strongly right-skewed variable?
options: To compress the long right tail and make the distribution closer to symmetric
To remove all outliers permanently and change nothing else
To make the mean equal the mode
questions.explain: A log transform shrinks large values more than small ones; in the lesson skewness fell from about 1.97 to about -0.47. It changes units, so interpret with care.
